t: Pataliputra grew from the village of Pataligrama into the capital of the Nanda, Maurya and Gupta empires, and at the confluence of the Ganges, Gandhaka and Son rivers it dominated the river trade of the Indo-Gangetic Plain.
Under Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE it was one of the largest cities in the world, with a wooden wall and 64 gates, and Megasthenes, a Greek ambassador, lived there and described it.

A shifting river, a decline in trade, a flood and perhaps an invasion ended its greatness, and by 637 Xuanzang found a ruined city with a small walled town of about 1,000 people; Sher Shah Suri later made the place his capital as Patna.
dyk: When the monk Faxian visited about 400 CE, he found that the city's nobles and householders had built hospitals where the poor, the crippled and the diseased of all countries received food, drink and medicines free of charge.
ev: Ajatashatru builds a fort at the village of Pataligrama, the beginning of the city
The Maurya Empire begins, and Pataliputra is its capital
Megasthenes mentions Pataliputra in his Indika
Under Ashoka the city holds about 150,000 to 400,000 people and a Buddhist council meets there
Faxian visits the Gupta capital and finds the people rich and prosperous
A flood on the Son River likely devastates the city
Xuanzang finds the old city in ruins and a small walled town on the bank of the Ganges
Sher Shah Suri makes the site his capital and renames it Patna

f.founded: Built by the Magadha ruler Ajatashatru in 490 BCE as a small fort, Pataligrama, near the Ganges; other sources credit Udayin or Udayabhadra with founding the city, and archaeology shows urban development no earlier than the 3rd or 4th century BCE.
f.where: At the confluence of the Ganges, Gandhaka and Son rivers, beside modern Patna in Bihar, India.
f.known: A water fort at a river confluence; capital of the Nandas, Mauryas and Guptas; Megasthenes' account of its wooden walls and 64 gates; Ashoka's Buddhist council; Faxian's hospitals; its decline and abandonment
f.today: Much of the ancient city lies buried beneath modern Patna, and parts of it have been excavated at Kumhrar, Bulandi Bagh and Agam Kuan.
